subject: Chemistry
title: Aconite: The Queen of Poisons
description: A micro-lesson that makes Aconite: The Queen of Poisons usable.

hook.text: Aconite, or wolfsbane, is so toxic that ancient warriors dipped their arrows in its extract.

buildup.text: The active compound aconitine binds to sodium channels in nerve and heart cells, keeping them permanently open.

discovery.text: Open sodium channels overstimulate nerves. Victims feel tingling, then burning, then cardiac arrhythmia sets in.

twist.text: There is no reliable antidote. Treatment is just managing symptoms and hoping the body clears the poison.

climax.text: In 2009, a UK woman was murdered with aconite curry. It was one of the first convictions for aconite poisoning.

punchline.text: Sodium channels forced open. Nerves fire until the heart gives out.

quiz.question: How does aconitine poison the body?
options: It locks sodium channels open, overstimulating nerves and the heart
It blocks all pain receptors permanently
It dissolves the myelin sheath around nerves

details.summary: Aconite from the monkshood plant contains aconitine, which activates voltage-gated sodium channels in nerve and heart cells, causing them to fire continuously. This leads to fatal cardiac arrhythmias, and death can occur within hours of ingestion with no reliable antidote.
details.whyItMatters: Aconite is one of the most toxic plant poisons in Europe and has been used in assassinations throughout history. Its mechanism informed the development of sodium channel pharmacology.
takeaways: Aconitine locks sodium channels open, causing continuous nerve firing
Death from cardiac arrhythmia can occur within hours of exposure
No specific antidote exists; treatment is entirely supportive

faq.question: Why is aconite considered more dangerous than many other plant poisons?
faq.answer: Aconitine is toxic through skin absorption as well as ingestion, making even handling the plant dangerous. The lethal dose is as low as two milligrams, there is no antidote, and the cardiac effects can be irreversible once established.

faq.question: How is aconite poisoning treated without a specific antidote?
faq.answer: Treatment focuses on managing cardiac arrhythmias with anti-arrhythmic drugs and life support. Activated charcoal can reduce absorption if given within the first hour. Some success has been reported with cardiopulmonary bypass to support the heart through the toxic period.
